A memory leak is sustained retention of memory that should have been released. Production symptoms often show resident memory rising across otherwise similar traffic windows, more frequent garbage collection, swap or OOM pressure, and recovery after restarting the leaking process. Investigation should compare heap growth with request volume, inspect retained object types, review caches and listener lifecycles, and distinguish a leak from an intentionally warm cache. Mitigations include bounding caches, removing stale references, closing resources, and deploying temporary restart protection while the retention path is fixed.

An N+1 query problem occurs when code fetches a collection and then performs an additional database query for each item. It appears as very high counts of similar single-row queries, latency increasing with list size, unnecessary network round trips, and database time dominated by repeated lookups. Confirm by tracing one request, grouping SQL by normalized statement, and comparing unbatched and batched call counts. Typical fixes are eager loading, joins, batch fetch APIs, prefetching, or restructuring the data-access layer so a list is resolved in a bounded number of queries.
